summary.name: Trayce
summary.one_liner: Trayce is a free, open-source API client and desktop GUI that also monitors network traffic from local Docker containers using eBPF.
use_cases: debug HTTP traffic between local Docker containers
test REST and GraphQL APIs locally
monitor gRPC, MySQL or PostgreSQL traffic in containers
run API tests with a collection runner
summary.what_it_does: Trayce is a desktop API client with a GUI that stores collections locally in the git-friendly bruno-lang format, with no account required. It supports HTTP, REST, and GraphQL requests, with authentication, JavaScript scripting, variables, secrets management, history, and OpenAPI import. A separate Trayce Agent container runs alongside existing Docker containers and uses eBPF probes to capture their network traffic, including TLS-encrypted traffic, and displays it in the GUI. It can also import gRPC protobuf files to decode messages. Bruno collections can be opened and edited in Trayce while remaining compatible with the Bruno app.
notable: Zero-config Docker traffic monitoring via eBPF, with no proxy or CA certificate setup needed
Interoperable with Bruno collections and the bruno-lang file format
Monitors HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, MySQL and PostgreSQL traffic
caveats: Some Bruno features are still being implemented (near-parity, not full parity)
HTTPS interception via eBPF is listed as supported for Go and OpenSSL-based languages such as Python and Ruby
